- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral (0.00–0.20) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent days.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of sharp decline), model tends to lag; shift forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment history includes 2+ positive signals (0.20+), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon; apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 7–10 days of forecast.  
- If true outcome shows volatility clustering (e.g., 3+ consecutive days with >2% swing), model tends to smooth too much; add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast.
